## Questions reported for Palantir

### [RAG and retrieval](../themes/rag-retrieval.md)

- **Design retrieval that enforces the source system's access rights, including permission changes and shared caches.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Databricks](databricks.md) †, [Microsoft](microsoft.md) †, [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether access checks cover the full path to generated output.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Propagate identity and enforce authorisation before content reaches the model.
    - Keep permission updates, deletions and cache keys consistent with the policy.
    - Test denied access and revocation paths; citations and logs need the same boundary.
  - Read: [Document-level access control](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/search/search-document-level-access-overview) (Microsoft Learn)
- **A user asks for the count of open orders blocked by supplier issues. Why might document retrieval fail, and what should answer the query?**
  - Applied scenario · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether structured aggregation is separated from semantic retrieval.

### [Agents, tools and protocols](../themes/agents-tools.md)

- **How would you make an agent's production actions reversible where possible and auditable where reversal is impossible?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether compensating actions and durable evidence are planned before execution.
- **Design human approval for consequential agent actions, including how approval remains bound to the exact action being executed.**
  - System design · Asked at: [OpenAI](openai.md) †, [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether approval controls are enforced outside the model.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Preview the concrete action, target and consequences before approval.
    - Bind approval to validated arguments and recheck authorisation at execution.
    - Record the decision and execution result; expire approval after material changes.
  - Read: [Building Effective AI Agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents) (Anthropic) · [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe)
- **Design an agent that creates and updates work orders in a live ERP without duplicating or silently corrupting business operations.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether business invariants survive uncertain model and network behaviour.
- **Why might an enterprise agent operate on an ontology of business objects and actions instead of raw tables and documents?**
  - Knowledge · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether semantic modelling is connected to valid operations and permissions.

### [Evaluation and observability](../themes/evals-observability.md)

- **How would you change evaluation when an LLM workflow moves from suggesting actions to executing them in production?**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether action consequences change the acceptance criteria.

### [AI system design](../themes/ai-system-design.md)

- **Design a pipeline that extracts structured fields from ten million scanned documents and makes uncertain results reviewable.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether extraction quality, provenance and scalable processing are planned together.
- **Design natural-language querying over a warehouse with thousands of tables, from schema selection to safe query execution.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Databricks](databricks.md) †, [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether semantic correctness and query permissions constrain generation.
- **Design an LLM gateway with provider routing, failover, caching, rate limits and enforceable spending budgets.**
  - System design · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †, [Perplexity](perplexity.md) †
  - Tests: Whether provider differences and failure handling preserve the service contract.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Define provider capabilities and normalise only compatible request semantics.
    - Enforce tenant quotas and budgets before dispatch, including retries.
    - Specify failover boundaries for partially streamed responses and side-effecting tool calls.
  - Read: [Scaling your API with rate limiters](https://stripe.com/blog/rate-limiters) (Stripe) · [Designing robust and predictable APIs with idempotency](https://stripe.com/blog/idempotency) (Stripe)

### [Practical coding](../themes/coding-practical.md)

- **Write a function that collects a paginated REST result while handling page size, termination and incomplete responses explicitly.**
  - Coding · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether boundary conditions prevent missing or duplicated records.

### [AI platform and operating model](../themes/ai-operating-model.md)

- **How would you support multiple model providers when some deployment environments permit only a subset of models?**
  - System design · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether a platform preserves deployment constraints and makes capability gaps visible.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Make environment policy and data restrictions explicit in model selection.
    - Define a portable interface without pretending all models have identical capabilities.
    - Evaluate allowed fallbacks and fail closed when no compliant route exists.
  - Read: [Architect multitenant solutions on Azure](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/architecture/guide/multitenant/overview) (Microsoft Learn) · [AI Risk Management Framework](https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework) (NIST)
- **Design a service that lets several teams query a shared dataset without exposing the underlying raw records.**
  - System design · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you define permissible results and enforce access across a shared platform.

### [Applied and customer scenarios](../themes/applied-scenarios.md)

- **A customer executive wants to cancel an AI pilot because it keeps producing wrong results. What would you do over the next 48 hours?**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you combine incident triage with a credible customer recovery plan.
  - A strong answer covers:
    - Acknowledge impact and collect concrete failing workflows with the customer.
    - Contain harmful behaviour and separate data, system and expectation problems.
    - Agree on a short recovery experiment and explicit continue-or-stop criteria.
  - Read: [Site Reliability Engineering](https://sre.google/sre-book/table-of-contents/) (Google) · [Demystifying evals for AI agents](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents) (Anthropic)
- **A freight railway loses substantial revenue to unexpected locomotive downtime. Turn the problem into an engineering plan.**
  - Applied scenario · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you connect operational decisions, usable data and intervention value.
- **How would you design a system to improve traffic in New York City?**
  - System design · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you decompose an ambiguous city-scale objective into measurable interventions.
- **Design synchronisation between two systems that hold employee records.**
  - System design · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you identify record ownership, conflicts and recovery semantics.
- **Design an application for recording species while exploring an unfamiliar environment.**
  - System design · Senior · Asked at: [Palantir](palantir.md) †
  - Tests: Whether you clarify field constraints and support trustworthy data collection.
